_transcription: ENGLISH half only, CBSE Class 10 Science (086), set 31/5/3 (Series CABD5/5), sibling of the opener 31/5/1. 27 page images, cover announces 27 printed pages. idx 0 cover, idx 1 Hindi instructions, idx 2 English instructions + Q1; English on EVERY EVEN index 2-26, Hindi on every odd index 3-25 (each the Hindi of the page after it); odd-page tops checked, all Hindi; last page idx 26 English (Q38(b) to Q39). Instructions confirm sci80: 39 questions, A Q1-20 MCQ (17-20 Assertion-Reason), B 21-26 x2, C 27-33 x3, D 34-36 x5, E 37-39 x4. plan.txt gives no skip list (no numbered scheme cells), so every question was matched by CONTENT against 2024-31-5-1: 29 of its questions recur here reshuffled, and their stem/context/options/answer/chapter/subtopic/difficulty are copied from the reference after reading each on this paper's own page. New to this set: Q3, Q20, Q22, Q24, Q25, Q26, Q27, Q29, Q32, Q36(a), Q36(b). Instruction (viii) prints NO count of internal choices, so the roster was built by walking the marking scheme (ms idx 2-9, every footer 'X SCIENCE 31/5/3'): a bare OR after Q21, 23, 33, 34, 35, 36, 37(c), 38(c), 39(c) = 9 alternatives, each confirmed against a printed OR on the paper. Q25, Q27 and Q32 carry lettered parts with NO OR (all compulsory). All 20 Section-A answers are CBSE's own, read off the scheme page image (ms idx 2); each was re-derived and agrees. No void or unconditional-award note anywhere in the scheme (the only note, Q37(c)(ii) 'Deduct 1/2 mark if direction of rays is not shown', is conditional). Decimal points on this paper are RAISED (Q26 0{\cdot}5 A, Q32 1{\cdot}0 A, Q36 4{\cdot}5 V and the table). Case studies print (a), (b), (c)(i) OR (c)(ii). Q36(a)(i) prints an em dash after 'circuits', kept in the stem as printed, as the A-R block and the Q37 passage keep theirs.

questions.stem: Sometimes while running, the athletes suffer from muscle cramps. Why ? How is the respiration in this case different from aerobic respiration ?
Write the other name given to lymph. State its two functions.
Write the formula and the molecular mass of the third homologue of alcohols. State how the boiling point of an alcohol changes as one moves from lower to higher homologues.
Copper powder is taken in a china dish and heated over a burner. Name the product formed and state its colour. Write the chemical equation for the reaction involved.

Write chemical equation for the chemical reaction which occurs when the aqueous solutions of barium chloride and sodium sulphate react together. Write the symbols of the ions present in the compound precipitated in the reaction.
Identify the organ in the human female reproductive system where the sperm encounters the egg cell. What will happen if it is blocked ? Name the technique by which it can be blocked.

“The linear magnification produced by a spherical mirror is \(+3\).” Based on this statement answer the following questions :

(a) What is the type of mirror ?

(b) Where is the object located ?

(c) List two properties of the image formed (other than the size/magnification).
The filament of an electric lamp draws a current of \(0{\cdot}5\) A, which lights for 2 hours. Calculate the charge that flows through the circuit.

Answer the following questions in the context of electrolysis of water :

(a) Why is this reaction/process called a decomposition reaction ?

(b) Giving reason state whether this reaction is exothermic or endothermic.

(c) Name the gases collected at the anode and cathode.

(d) What is the mass ratio of the gases collected at the anode and cathode ?

Differentiate between food chain and food web. In a food chain consisting of deer, grass and tiger, if the population of deer decreases, what will happen to the population of organisms belonging to the first and third trophic levels ?
Name a plant growth hormone synthesized at the shoot tip. Explain its effect on the growth of a plant in response to light.

Name the ore of mercury and state the form in which it is found in nature. Write the chemical equations along with the condition required for the reactions involved in the extraction of mercury from its ore.

Mendel crossed pure tall pea plants (TT) with pure short pea plants (tt) and obtained \(\mathrm{F_1}\) progeny. When the plants of \(\mathrm{F_1}\) progeny were self-pollinated, plants of \(\mathrm{F_2}\) progeny were obtained.

(a) What did the plants of \(\mathrm{F_1}\) progeny look like ? Give their gene combination.

(b) Why could the gene for shortness not be expressed in plants of \(\mathrm{F_1}\) progeny ?

(c) Write the ratio of the plants obtained in \(\mathrm{F_2}\) progeny and state the conclusion that can be drawn from this experiment.

A 2000 W heater has a resistance of about \(25\,\Omega\), whereas a 100 W bulb has a resistance of \(500\,\Omega\). When 220 V is applied on these, then which of the two

(a) can carry large currents ?

(b) may be used with an electrical circuit having \(1{\cdot}0\) A rating ?

(c) will be fitted with a 15 A electric board and not with a 5 A electric board ?

Justify your answer in each case.

(i) In the experimental set-up shown above in diagram (I) atmospheric air is being passed into lime water with a syringe while in diagram (II) air is being exhaled into lime water. The time taken for the lime water to turn milky in both the test tubes is different. Give reason.
